title: Slimline adaptor deprecation: compatibility shim, migration constraints, and rollback criteria
creator: Aisha Banerjee
summary: This ticket defines the Product Requirements and acceptance criteria for removing the legacy 'slimline' client adaptor/endpoint used by older SDKs and self-hosted integrations. The goal is to give customers a predictable, low-friction migration path to the unified /inference API while retiring the slimline compatibility layer and its server-side adapter. Includes rollout gates, telemetry thresholds, SDK guidance, and explicit rollback criteria.
background: Slimline adaptor was introduced as a lightweight compatibility layer in 2022 to bridge early SDKs to new generate/chat changes. Over time we have accumulated special-case behaviors and maintenance overhead in runtime and routing logic. Removing slimline reduces operational complexity, enables consistent kernel selection, and simplifies telemetry. Several Enterprise customers still use the adaptor indirectly via older SDK versions.
scope_included: Implement a server-side compatibility shim (temporary) that returns structured deprecation headers and warning payloads when slimline requests are received
Define a phased migration timeline (shadow -> opt-in -> enforced) and acceptance gates tied to telemetry
Deliver SDK update notes, migration checklist, and automated client-detection telemetry tags
Provide a CLI-based validation tool for customers to test requests against unified endpoints
Create an emergency rollback plan and operational runbook for incidents during ramp
out_of_scope: Rewriting customer application logic — we provide guidance and tooling but not custom rewrites
Major changes to model aliasing policies — model sunsets handled by separate PRDs
Extensive on-prem appliance changes beyond compatibility shim behavior
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility shim responds to legacy slimline requests with HTTP 200 and a defined 'Deprecation-Notice' header and body explaining migration by 2026-04-01
Telemetry shows at least 85% of slimline-originated requests identified by client header or SDK fingerprint within first 2 weeks of shadowing
At least 90% of active slimline clients have received a migration notification (email/console+header) prior to opt-in enforcement phase
Automated migration validator CLI (redwood-migrate v0.1) verifies request parity for 80% of sampled legacy integrations
Rollout proceeds to enforced rejection (HTTP 410) only after meeting safety gates defined in telemetry_gates
Acceptance tests (integration suite) include negative cases for header presence, correct fallback behavior, and documented error codes
Engineering has a tested rollback that restores prior routing behavior within the 15-minute SLA under the operational runbook
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Announcement (2026-03-15): Publish migration timeline and docs; email impacted customers; open support channel
Phase 1 - Shadow (2026-03-22 -> 2026-04-05): Enable compatibility shim in shadow mode for 2 weeks; collect parity and error rates; do not alter customer traffic paths
Phase 2 - Advisory (2026-04-06 -> 2026-05-03): Shim returns Deprecation-Notice header and response body advising migration; provide CLI validator and SDK patches; monitor uptake

Phase 3 - Opt-in Enforcement (2026-05-04 -> 2026-05-31): Default routing prefers unified endpoint; slimline requests can opt-in to compatibility with feature flag for customers who explicitly enabled it
Phase 4 - Enforced Retirement (target 2026-06-01): Slimline endpoints return HTTP 410 (Gone) with migration instructions; post-mortem window open for high-impact customers
Post-retirement - Cleanup (2026-06-01 -> 2026-07-01): Remove shim code paths, clean telemetry, and update runtime docs
telemetry_gates: Parity error rate (shim vs unified) < 0.5% over 72h before moving from Shadow -> Advisory
Overall customer error increase attributable to migration < 0.3% (service-level) during Advisory window
At least 70% of traffic from top-50 impacted customers validated by migration CLI before Opt-in Enforcement
No severe incidents (P0) caused by shim interactions in last 7 days before Enforced Retirement
rollback_criteria: If overall 5xx rate attributable to slimline path increases by more than 250% relative to baseline in any rolling 1-hour window, initiate immediate rollback
If more than 5% of authenticated enterprise requests receive unexpected payload changes during enforcement phase, pause rollout and rollback
If more than two named customers request emergency rollback within 24 hours and demonstrate production impact, trigger customer-specific rollbacks and prioritize follow-up
Rollback must restore full prior routing behavior and compatibility headers within 15 minutes and notify on-call and PM
engineering_requirements: Add 'Deprecation-Notice' response header and standard JSON body with migration_url and migration_id fields for all shim responses
Feature flag: runtime.feature.slimline_compat with modes {shadow, advisory, optin, disabled} controllable at org-level
SDKs must be updated to start emitting 'X-Client-Signature: slimline-vX' by 2026-04-01; server will use this for client mapping
Compatibility shim must log both original and normalized request fingerprints for parity analysis; log schema must conform to telemetry spec v2
Create endpoint /internal/migrate/validate (auth-required) used by the CLI validator to return a parity score
Enforced retirement must return HTTP 410 with structured error code 'SLIMLINE_DEPRECATED' and include migration_id in response
docs_and_sdk_changes: Upgrade notes for SDKs (python/node/java) with code snippets and automated fixers
Release CLI validator (redwood-migrate v0.1) and publish in GitHub Releases
Create Console banner and per-org inbox notifications for impacted customers
Update API reference to remove slimline-specific behaviors post-cleanup
test_plan: Integration tests that exercise legacy header permutations and assert normalized output parity
Chaos test during Shadow phase that simulates dropped connections and high latency to evaluate shim resilience
Customer-replay tests for top-20 impacted customers using captured requests in a sandbox
End-to-end QA runbook for on-call to follow during each phase (checklists + dashboards)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large customers rely on undocumented slimline behavior -> Mitigation: Prioritize outreach and offer migration engineering sessions
Risk: Parity gaps between shim and unified runtime -> Mitigation: Extend Shadow window and add more parity logging; require >95% parity in critical paths
Risk: SDK adoption lags -> Mitigation: Provide backport patches and automated rewrite scripts; keep opt-in feature flag for limited customers
Risk: Unexpected security or auth regressions -> Mitigation: On-call security review during Advisory and Opt-in phases; quick rollback path
